resource.name: aws_glacier_vault
resource.description: Provides a Glacier Vault Resource. You can refer to the Glacier Developer Guide for a full explanation of the Glacier Vault functionality When removing a Glacier Vault, the Vault must be empty.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_glacier_vault` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of Amazon Glacier Vaults for secure, cost-effective long-term data archiving and backup. It is commonly used for scenarios requiring cold storage of infrequently accessed data, compliance with data retention policies, or disaster recovery planning. Users can configure vault access policies, lifecycle rules for data retention, and ensure the vault is empty before deletion, supporting efficient and compliant data management workflows.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_glacier_vault` with an SNS notification system for specific events (`ArchiveRetrievalCompleted`, `InventoryRetrievalCompleted`) and an IAM access policy allowing read-only permissions for Glacier jobs. It showcases the use of the `notification` block, integration with an `aws_sns_topic`, and the `access_policy` argument to control access to the vault.

arguments.name: access_policy
arguments.description: (Optional) The policy document. This is a JSON formatted string. The heredoc syntax or `file` function is helpful here. Use the Glacier Developer Guide for more information on Glacier Vault Policy
arguments.llm_summary: The `access_policy` argument for the `aws_glacier_vault` resource allows users to define a JSON-formatted policy document that specifies access control rules for the Glacier Vault, such as permissions for IAM users, roles, or external accounts. By configuring this argument, users can enforce fine-grained access management, ensuring secure and compliant data access in alignment with organizational or regulatory requirements.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_glacier_vault` resource represents the unique identifier of the Glacier vault, typically auto-generated by Terraform upon creation. While optional, specifying this argument allows users to reference the vault explicitly in other resources or outputs, enabling integration and management workflows that depend on the vault's unique identity.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the Vault. Names can be between 1 and 255 characters long and the valid characters are a-z, A-Z, 0-9, '_' (underscore), '-' (hyphen), and '.' (period).
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_glacier_vault` resource specifies the unique identifier for the Glacier Vault, allowing users to define a human-readable name that adheres to specific character constraints. Setting this argument is essential for creating and managing the vault, as it serves as the primary reference for operations like data archiving, retrieval, and lifecycle configuration within AWS Glacier.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level. notification supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_glacier_vault` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the Glacier vault, enabling organization, categorization, and identification of the resource for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or automation workflows. When configured, these tags can override provider-level default tags, ensuring granular control over resource-specific tagging.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_glacier_vault` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically propagated to the vault, enabling consistent metadata management across AWS resources. By configuring this argument, users can streamline resource categorization, improve cost allocation, and enhance searchability for auditing or organizational purposes.

blocks.name: notification
blocks.description: (Optional) The notifications for the Vault. Fields documented below.

arguments.name: events
arguments.description: (Required) You can configure a vault to publish a notification for `ArchiveRetrievalCompleted` and `InventoryRetrievalCompleted` events.
arguments.llm_summary: The `events` argument in the `notification` configuration of the `aws_glacier_vault` resource allows users to specify which types of events (`ArchiveRetrievalCompleted` and `InventoryRetrievalCompleted`) should trigger notifications for the vault. By defining this argument, users enable event-driven workflows, ensuring timely alerts or actions when specific data retrieval operations are completed in Amazon Glacier.

arguments.name: sns_topic
arguments.llm_summary: The `sns_topic` argument specifies the Amazon SNS Topic ARN to which Glacier vault notifications are sent, enabling users to configure event-driven workflows or alerting mechanisms for vault operations such as archive retrieval or deletion. By setting this required argument, users can integrate their Glacier vault with external systems for monitoring or automation purposes, aligning with common goals like event notification and system orchestration.

blocks.llm_summary: The `notification` configuration block in the `aws_glacier_vault` resource enables the setup of event notifications for the Glacier Vault, allowing users to define how and where notifications are sent when specific vault events occur. This block encapsulates settings related to event types, SNS topics, and delivery configurations, helping users integrate Glacier Vault operations with external systems for monitoring or automation purposes.

attributes.name: location
attributes.description: The URI of the vault that was created.
